zh-CN.title: 让经文自己发声
zh-CN.body:
**让经文自己发声**

---

## 神，常常用问题开始

圣经中，神并不总是先给答案。

祂常常先问。

> “你在哪里？”（创世记 3:9）
> “你兄弟亚伯在哪里？”（创世记 4:9）
> “你在这里做什么？”（列王纪上 19:9）

祂当然知道答案。

但祂仍然问，
因为人还没有面对自己。

在约伯记中，神甚至用一连串问题：

> “我立大地根基的时候，你在哪里呢？”（约伯记 38:4）

不是为了压倒人，
而是让人看见：

- 人的有限
- 神的广大

---

## 主耶稣，用问题带人进入真理

主耶稣极少急着给结论。

祂问：

> “你们说我是谁？”（马太福音 16:15）
> “你要痊愈吗？”（约翰福音 5:6）
> “要我为你做什么？”（路加福音 18:41）

祂不是在测试人，
而是在邀请回应。

祂也问：

> “你们没有念过吗？”（马太福音 12:3）

不是增加讨论，
而是把人带回圣经。

祂甚至改变问题本身：

> “谁是我的邻舍？”（路加福音 10:29）
> “你想，这三个人哪一个是邻舍呢？”（路加福音 10:36）

不是给出定义，
而是翻转视角。

---

## 使徒与先知，也在用问题引导人

保罗写信时，不断发问：

> “这样，我们可说什么呢？”（罗马书 8:31）
> “难道神有什么不公平吗？”（罗马书 9:14）
> “我们可以仍在罪中，叫恩典显多吗？”（罗马书 6:1）

这些问题不是疑惑，
而是引导。

先知也是如此：

> “他指望结好葡萄，怎么倒结了野葡萄呢？”（以赛亚书 5:1–4）

问题，不只是表达，
而是进入人心。

---

## 问题，是进入真理的路径

从旧约到新约：

- 神
- 主耶稣
- 先知
- 使徒

我们看到一件一致的事：

> 从圣经中，我们看到神不仅用宣告，
> 也借着问题带领人进入真理。

---

## 但人回应的方式，并不一样

圣经让我们看到两种不同的属灵状态。

---

### 庇哩亚人（使徒行传 17:10–11）

他们听见信息，
没有急着接受，
也没有轻易否定。

他们做了一件简单却极少见的事：

> 天天查考圣经，要晓得这道是与不是。（使徒行传 17:11）

他们的特点不是“更聪明”，
而是：

- 回到经文
- 查考
- 辨明

---

### 哥林多教会

他们同样属灵资源丰富：

- 恩赐充足（林前 1:5–7；12:4–11）
- 知识丰富

但同时：

- 有纷争（林前 1:10–12）
- 有分党（林前 3:3–4）
- 属肉体（林前 3:1–3）

他们热衷表达，
却不一定停下来分辨；（林前 14:26–33）

他们有很多，
却不一定扎根在经文里。（林前 4:6）

---

## 这不是两间教会的差别

而是两种路径：

### 一种路径：

- 回到经文
- 查考
- 让经文判断一切

（使徒行传 17:11）

### 另一种路径：

- 拥有很多
- 经历很多
- 却没有根基

（哥林多前书 3:1–3）

---

> 问题不在于我们有没有经历，
> 而在于——
> 我们是否让经文成为判断一切的标准。（林前 4:6）

---

## 也许问题不在我们学得不够

而在于——
**我们是否真正进入过经文？**

我们活在一个信息极其丰富的时代。

关于圣经的内容，从不缺少：

- 讲道
- 解经
- 总结

我们可以听很多，
知道很多，
甚至谈论很多。

但仍然可能：

> 熟悉内容，
> 却没有进入经文。

---

## 我们正在失去的，不是知识

而是——进入

很多时候，我们读经：

- 快速得到答案
- 接受整理好的理解
- 停在别人的语言里

在我们看来，读经的路径是：

> 先进入，
> 再看见。

---

## 我们所做的，不是提供答案

我们不替代经文，
我们把人带回经文。

我们所提供的，只是一个入口：

> 问题

---

## 但问题，不是标准答案

它只是开始。

很多真正触及人心的问题，
不是预先写好的，
而是在读经中，
在安静中，
在光照中慢慢显出来的。

我们相信：

> 有些问题，
> 只有在经文面前，
> 才会被看见。

---

## 因此，这不只是一个工具

也是一个邀请

我们邀请你：

- 不只是使用问题
- 也在读经中发现问题

不只是接受整理好的理解
也在光中，领受新的看见

---

## 一起参与这件事

我们所整理的问题，
不是终点。

它们可以被补充，
被修正，
被更新。

当你在读经中：

- 看见一个真实的问题
- 一个触及生命的问题

你也可以把它带进来。

---

> 让问题，
> 不只是被使用，
> 也在群体中被发现。

---

## 一种庇哩亚式的查经

- 不是依赖解释，而是主动查考
- 不是停在听见，而是进入验证
- 不是快速得到，而是认真看见

---

## 让经文自己发声

当人真正回到经文：

> 解释不再是中心，
> 经文开始说话。

---

## 一句话

> 我们不是给你答案，
> 而是带你进入经文。

> 我们不是解释圣经，
> 而是让你亲自看见。

---

## 邀请

如果你愿意：

- 不只是知道，而是查考
- 不只是听见，而是看见
- 不只是理解，而是回应

欢迎你进入：

> 让经文自己发声的读经方式

en.title: Let Scripture Speak
en.body:
**Let Scripture Speak**

---

## God Often Begins with Questions

In Scripture, God does not always give the answer first.

He often asks first.

> “Where are you?” (Genesis 3:9)
> “Where is Abel your brother?” (Genesis 4:9)
> “What are you doing here?” (1 Kings 19:9)

He already knows the answer.

Yet He still asks,
because the person has not yet faced themselves.

In Job, God even asks a long series of questions:

> “Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth?” (Job 38:4)

Not to overwhelm the person,
but to help them see:

- human limits
- God’s vastness

---

## The Lord Jesus Leads People into Truth through Questions

The Lord Jesus rarely rushed to a conclusion.

He asked:

> “Who do you say that I am?” (Matthew 16:15)
> “Do you want to be healed?” (John 5:6)
> “What do you want me to do for you?” (Luke 18:41)

He was not testing people,
but inviting a response.

He also asked:

> “Have you not read?” (Matthew 12:3)

Not to add more discussion,
but to bring people back to Scripture.

He even changed the question itself:

> “Who is my neighbor?” (Luke 10:29)
> “Which of these three, do you think, was neighbor to him?” (Luke 10:36)

Not to give a definition,
but to turn the perspective.

---

## Apostles and Prophets Also Guide through Questions

When Paul wrote his letters, he kept asking:

> “What then shall we say to these things?” (Romans 8:31)
> “Is there injustice on God’s part?” (Romans 9:14)
> “Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound?” (Romans 6:1)

These questions are not doubt,
but guidance.

The prophets did the same:

> “He looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes.” (Isaiah 5:1–4)

Questions are not only expression,
but a way into the heart.

---

## Questions Are a Path into Truth

From Old Testament to New:

- God
- the Lord Jesus
- the prophets
- the apostles

We see one consistent pattern:

> In Scripture we see that God not only declares,
> but also leads people into truth through questions.

---

## Yet People Respond in Different Ways

Scripture shows us two different spiritual postures.

---

### The Bereans (Acts 17:10–11)

They heard the message,
did not rush to accept it,
and did not easily dismiss it either.

They did something simple yet rare:

> They received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so. (Acts 17:11)

Their distinction was not being “smarter,”
but:

- returning to Scripture
- searching
- discerning

---

### The Church in Corinth

They too were rich in spiritual resources:

- gifts in abundance (1 Corinthians 1:5–7; 12:4–11)
- much knowledge

Yet at the same time:

- divisions (1 Corinthians 1:10–12)
- factions (1 Corinthians 3:3–4)
- spiritual immaturity (1 Corinthians 3:1–3)

They were eager to express themselves,
but did not necessarily stop to discern; (1 Corinthians 14:26–33)

They had much,
but were not necessarily rooted in Scripture. (1 Corinthians 4:6)

---

## This Is Not the Difference between Two Churches

It is the difference between two paths:

### One path:

- return to Scripture
- search
- let Scripture judge everything

(Acts 17:11)

### Another path:

- have much
- experience much
- yet lack a foundation

(1 Corinthians 3:1–3)

---

> The issue is not whether we have experience,
> but whether—
> we let Scripture become the standard by which everything is judged. (1 Corinthians 4:6)

---

## Perhaps the Problem Is Not That We Have Not Learned Enough

But whether—
**we have truly entered into Scripture.**

We live in an age of extraordinary abundance of information.

Content about the Bible is never lacking:

- sermons
- commentaries
- summaries

We can listen to much,
know much,
even talk much.

And still:

> be familiar with content,
> yet never enter Scripture itself.

---

## What We Are Losing Is Not Knowledge

But—entry

Often when we read Scripture, we:

- quickly get an answer
- accept a ready-made understanding
- stop in someone else’s language

In our view, the path of reading Scripture is:

> enter first,
> then see.

---

## What We Do Is Not Provide Answers

We do not replace Scripture;
we bring people back to Scripture.

What we offer is only an entry point:

> a question

---

## But a Question Is Not a Standard Answer

It is only a beginning.

Many questions that truly reach the heart
are not written in advance,
but emerge in reading,
in quiet,
in light.

We believe:

> some questions
> are seen only
> before Scripture.

---

## Therefore, This Is Not Only a Tool

It is also an invitation.

We invite you:

- not only to use questions
- but to discover questions in reading

not only to accept ready-made understanding
but to receive new sight in the light

---

## Join in This Work

The questions we have gathered
are not the end.

They can be added to,
corrected,
updated.

When in your reading you:

- see a real question
- a question that touches life

you may bring it in as well.

---

> Let questions
> not only be used,
> but also be discovered in community.

---

## A Berean-Style Study

- not relying on explanation, but searching actively
- not stopping at hearing, but entering into verification
- not seeking quick gain, but seeing carefully

---

## Let Scripture Speak

When people truly return to Scripture:

> explanation is no longer the center;
> Scripture begins to speak.

---

## In One Sentence

> We are not giving you answers;
> we are bringing you into Scripture.

> We are not explaining the Bible for you;
> we are helping you see for yourself.

---

## An Invitation

If you are willing:

- not only to know, but to search
- not only to hear, but to see
- not only to understand, but to respond

you are welcome to enter:

> a way of reading Scripture that lets Scripture speak

---

zh-CN.title: 圣经中的查经模型
zh-CN.body:
# 读经

## 前言：我们遇到的问题与挑战

- 读经枯燥，找不到从圣经学习领受的路径
- 时间被充满了，却很少留下来对圣经话语的扎根
- 容易从别人已经总结的、主题式的、领受式的内容中学习
 - 因为这样简单好懂
 - 却不容易从圣经本身来学习
 - 当传授的人领受错误，我们也会被错误引导

---

## 一、圣经中的查经模型

### 1. 旧约的模式（尼希米记 8:8）

> “他们清清楚楚地念神的律法书，讲明意思，使百姓明白。”

#### 三个步骤：

1. **读**
 - 人：接触神的话
 - 圣灵：吸引进入

2. **解释**
 - 人：观察与理解
 - 圣灵：防止偏差

3. **明白**
 - 人：进入真理
 - 圣灵：开启心眼

> 我们认为，真正的“明白”不只是分析出来的，更是被开启的

---

### 2. 耶稣的示范（路加福音 24章）

以马忤斯路上的查经方式：

1. **先问问题**
 - “你们在谈什么？”
 - 引导观察 / 暴露状态

2. **倾听他们的理解（即使是错的）**
 - 接纳理解 / 预备人心

3. **用整本圣经解释**
 - 从摩西到先知
 - 真理进入

4. **让他们心被开启**
 - 圣灵点亮

#### 小结：
> 不是直接给答案
> 而是：引导 + 解释 + 点亮

我们认为查经目标不只是“讲清楚”，更是“心被点燃”

---

### 3. 庇哩亚人的榜样（使徒行传 17:10–15）

- 听道
- 天天查考圣经验证
- 主动参与

#### 对应关系：
- 人：天天查考、主动验证
- 圣灵：使人看见、给里面确认

> 我们认为，查经不只是被动听，更是主动验证

## 17:11
> 甘心领受这道，天天考查圣经，要晓得这道是与不是

---

### 4. 保罗的门徒训练模式

1. 教导真理（提后 2:2）
2. 生活榜样（林前 11:1）
3. 使命托付（提后 2:2）

#### 小结：
- 查经不仅是知识
- 而是生命复制

不是培养“好基督徒”，而是“可复制的门徒”

---
## 二、请求圣灵参与在我们的读经中

> 在我们看来，读经不只是“理解一本书”，更是在圣灵里，让神对我们说话

### 1. 圣灵开启理解
- 路加福音 24章
 - 耶稣讲解圣经
 - 门徒说：“心里火热”
 - “他们的心眼被开启”

### 2. 圣灵教导并提醒
- 约翰福音 14章
 - 圣灵要教导你们
 - 并且叫你们想起我对你们所说的一切话
 - 教导
 - 提醒

### 3. 圣灵引导进入真理
- 约翰福音 16章
 - 圣灵要引导你们明白一切的真理

- 关键理解：
 - 引导不是一次性告诉，而是过程式带领
 - 读经不是一次完成，而是不断被带领深入
 - “心里火热 → 心眼被开启”
 - 理解圣经不仅是信息理解，而是被开启

### 4. 圣灵使人能领受属灵的事
- 哥林多前书 2章
 - 属血气的人不领会神圣灵的事
 - 唯有属灵的人才能看透

- 关键：
 - 圣经不是普通文本
 - 若觉得“普通、没感觉”，往往是缺少圣灵开启

### 5. 圣灵光照
- 以弗所书 1章
 - 求神照明你们心中的眼睛

- 不是：
 - 逻辑理解
- 而是：
 - 属灵看见

> 有时候同一节经文突然“有光”，就是光照

### 6. 圣灵使话语成为生命
- 约翰福音 6章
 - “我对你们所说的话，就是灵，就是生命”

- 圣经不是知识，而是生命载体
- 圣灵使它“活起来”

---

### 总结：圣灵的工作
**开启、教导、提醒、引导、光照**

- 我们相信，圣灵通常不是跳过圣经直接说话
- 而是通过圣经本身说话
- 这样可以避免被误导（因为魔鬼是说谎之父）

---

### 实际操练

- 读经前：
 > 主啊，求你借着圣灵开启我，让我明白你的话

- 读经时：
 - 慢一点
 - 注意重复
 - 留意触动你的地方

- 读完后：
 - 这段话对我今天有什么意义？

---

## 三、小组查经实操

### 1. 破冰
- 心被打开

---

### 2. 读经
- 让经文本身先说话

---

### 3. 观察（不解释）

- 看到了什么？
- 有什么重复？
- 有什么特别的词？
- 有没有词“跳出来”？

#### 核心原则：
- 用问题引出**事实**，不是解释

#### 正确流程：
> 问 → 听 → 放大 → 再问 → 汇总 → 进入下一层

收集 → 放大 → 整理

---

### 4. 解释（真理被看见）

#### 常用问题：
1. 神在这段经文中做了什么？
2. 人为什么这样做？
3. 这段经文在强调什么？
4. 为什么作者要记录？
5. 与上下文、整本圣经有什么关系？

#### 操作步骤：
1. 从观察“收口”
2. 先问大问题
3. 再问具体问题
4. 带领者负责整理，不包办答案

#### 关键提醒：
- 控制方向，但不要讲道
- 没有圣灵 → 容易变成人的理解
- 不只解释“人做了什么”
- 一定要看到“神在做什么”

---

### 5. 应用（被光照）

- 必须具体
- 这对我本周有什么影响？
- 我要改变什么？

圣灵光照真实状态

## 以弗所书 1章
> 照明心中的眼睛

> “这段话就是在说我”

#### 关键：
- 没有应用 = 只有知识积累

---

### 6. 祷告（圣灵内化）

> 在我们看来，查经不只是信息流动，更是圣灵在运行

---

## 四、带领者的关键原则

### 1. 身份：引导者，不是讲员
- 错误：一直讲
- 正确：一直问

> 在我们看来，改变人的不是我，而是圣灵

---

### 2. 问题比答案更重要
- 开放式问题
- 可讨论
- 引导思考

通过问题，让圣灵说话

---

### 3. 允许安静
- 不急着填空
- 思考时间 = 属灵空间
- 给圣灵工作的时间

---

### 4. 控制跑题
- 一句话拉回：
 > 我们回到经文本身

---

### 5. 平衡点

- 只有方法 → 理性但无生命
- 只等感动 → 不读经、不观察

- 正确：
 > 用耶稣示范的方法读经，在圣灵中被开启

en.title: Models of Bible Study in Scripture
en.body:
# Bible Reading

## Preface: The Problems and Challenges We Face

- Bible reading feels dry; it is hard to find a path of learning and receiving from Scripture
- Time is full, yet little remains for rooting ourselves in God’s word
- It is easy to learn from what others have already summarized—topical content, devotional takeaways
 - because it is simple and clear
 - yet hard to learn from Scripture itself
 - when the one teaching has received something wrongly, we are led wrongly too

---



## I. Models of Bible Study in Scripture

### 1. The Old Testament Pattern (Nehemiah 8:8)

> “They read from the book, from the Law of God, clearly, and they gave the sense, so that the people understood the reading.”

#### Three steps:

1. **Read**
 - People: encounter God’s word
 - Holy Spirit: draw us in

2. **Explain**
 - People: observe and understand
 - Holy Spirit: guard against drift

3. **Understand**
 - People: enter into truth
 - Holy Spirit: open the eyes of the heart

> In our view, true “understanding” is not only worked out by analysis; it is also opened

---

### 2. Jesus’ Example (Luke 24)

The way of study on the road to Emmaus:

1. **Ask questions first**
 - “What are you discussing?”
 - guide observation / reveal where people are

2. **Listen to their understanding (even when it is wrong)**
 - receive their understanding / prepare the heart

3. **Explain from all of Scripture**
 - from Moses to the prophets
 - truth enters in

4. **Let their hearts be opened**
 - the Holy Spirit brings light

#### Summary:
> not giving the answer directly
> but: guide + explain + illuminate

We believe the goal of Bible study is not only to “explain clearly,” but to have hearts set on fire

---

### 3. The Bereans’ Example (Acts 17:10–15)

- hear the word
- search the Scriptures daily to verify
- participate actively

#### Correspondence:
- People: search daily, verify actively
- Holy Spirit: help people see, give inner confirmation

> In our view, Bible study is not only passive listening, but active verification

## 17:11
> They received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures daily to see if these things were so.

---

### 4. Paul’s Disciple-Making Pattern

1. Teach truth (2 Timothy 2:2)
2. Live as an example (1 Corinthians 11:1)
3. Entrust the mission (2 Timothy 2:2)

#### Summary:
- Bible study is not only knowledge
- but the reproduction of life

Not forming “good Christians,” but reproducible disciples

---
## II. Asking the Holy Spirit to Join Our Reading

> In our view, reading Scripture is not only “understanding a book,” but in the Holy Spirit, letting God speak to us

### 1. The Holy Spirit Opens Understanding
- Luke 24
 - Jesus explained the Scriptures
 - the disciples said: “Were not our hearts burning?”
 - “Their eyes were opened”

### 2. The Holy Spirit Teaches and Reminds
- John 14
 - the Spirit will teach you
 - and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you
 - teaching
 - reminding

### 3. The Holy Spirit Guides into Truth
- John 16
 - the Spirit will guide you into all the truth

- Key understanding:
 - guidance is not a one-time telling, but a process of leading
 - reading Scripture is not finished once, but continually led deeper
 - “hearts burning → eyes opened”
 - understanding Scripture is not only grasping information, but being opened

### 4. The Holy Spirit Enables Receiving Spiritual Things
- 1 Corinthians 2
 - the natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God
 - only the spiritual person judges all things

- Key:
 - Scripture is not ordinary text
 - if it feels “ordinary, without impact,” often what is missing is the Spirit’s opening

### 5. The Holy Spirit Illuminates
- Ephesians 1
 - ask that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened

- not:
 - logical understanding alone
- but:
 - spiritual sight

> Sometimes the same verse suddenly “has light”—that is illumination

### 6. The Holy Spirit Makes the Word Life
- John 6
 - “The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and life”

- Scripture is not knowledge, but a carrier of life
- the Spirit makes it “come alive”

---

### Summary: The Work of the Holy Spirit
**Opening, teaching, reminding, guiding, illuminating**

- We believe the Spirit usually does not speak by bypassing Scripture
- but speaks through Scripture itself
- this helps us avoid being misled (for the devil is the father of lies)

---

### Practical Exercise

- Before reading:
 > Lord, by your Spirit open me, that I may understand your word

- While reading:
 - go slower
 - notice repetition
 - notice what touches you

- After reading:
 - what does this passage mean for me today?

---

## III. Small Group Bible Study in Practice

### 1. Opening
- hearts opened

---

### 2. Read Scripture
- let Scripture speak first

---

### 3. Observation (without explanation)

- What do you see?
- What repeats?
- What words stand out?
- Is there a word that “jumps out”?

#### Core principle:
- use questions to draw out **facts**, not explanation

#### Correct flow:
> ask → listen → amplify → ask again → summarize → go deeper

gather → amplify → organize

---

### 4. Interpretation (truth seen)

#### Common questions:
1. What is God doing in this passage?
2. Why did the people act this way?
3. What is this passage emphasizing?
4. Why did the author record this?
5. How does it relate to context and to all of Scripture?

#### Steps:
1. gather from observation
2. ask the big questions first
3. then ask specific questions
4. the leader organizes, but does not supply all the answers

#### Key reminders:
- guide direction, but do not preach
- without the Spirit → it easily becomes human understanding
- do not only explain “what people did”
- always see “what God is doing”

---

### 5. Application (being illuminated)

- must be concrete
- how does this affect me this week?
- what will I change?

the Spirit illuminates our real condition

## Ephesians 1
> enlighten the eyes of your heart

> “This passage is speaking about me”

#### Key:
- without application = knowledge accumulation only

---

### 6. Prayer (the Spirit internalizes)

> In our view, Bible study is not only the flow of information, but the Spirit at work

---

## IV. Key Principles for Leaders

### 1. Identity: guide, not lecturer
- wrong: keep talking
- right: keep asking

> In our view, what changes people is not me, but the Spirit

---

### 2. Questions matter more than answers
- open questions
- discussable
- guide thinking

through questions, let the Spirit speak

---

### 3. Allow silence
- do not rush to fill the space
- time to think = spiritual space
- give the Spirit time to work

---

### 4. Keep the group on track
- one sentence to return:
 > let us return to Scripture itself

---

### 5. Balance

- method only → rational but without life
- waiting for feeling only → no reading, no observation

- right:
 > read Scripture in the way Jesus modeled, and be opened by the Spirit

zh-CN.title: 关于读经计划的思考
zh-CN.body:
# 回到神的话语

## 读经计划

> “惟喜爱耶和华的律法，昼夜思想，这人便为有福。”
> ——《诗篇》1:2

> “人活着，不是单靠食物，乃是靠神口里所出的一切话。”
> ——《马太福音》4:4

很多人开始读经时，
都希望：

* 更认识神；
* 更亲近神；
* 更认真地读完整本圣经。

但慢慢地，
读经却很容易变成：

* 打卡；
* 任务；
* 进度；
* 压力。

于是：

* 落后会内疚；
* 中断会放弃；
* 读不完会觉得失败。

我们认为，读经更深的目的，
从来不只是：

# “完成阅读”。

在我们看来，神的话语
与其说为了增加宗教知识，

更是为了：

# 带领人回到与神爱的关系里。

> “你要尽心、尽性、尽意爱主你的神。”
> ——《马太福音》22:37

因此，

我们希望建立的，
不是一种：

# “快速完成圣经”的计划，

而是一种：

# 长期、稳定、真实与神同行的生活节奏。

---

# 我们的方法论

## 1. 三循环系统

### 解决：长期读经失衡、疲劳、容易中断的问题

很多人读经失败，
不是因为不爱神，

而是因为长期只读一种内容。

例如：

* 连续读旧约会疲惫；
* 连续读律法会沉重；
* 只读熟悉经文又会停滞。

因此我们采用：

* 旧约
* 新约
* 智慧书

同时进行的方式。

旧约帮助我们认识神的计划与根基；

新约不断把生命带回基督与福音的中心；

智慧书帮助我们祷告、默想，并真实地与神同行。

---

## 2. 不打卡、不赶进度

### 解决：内疚、压力、放弃的问题

很多读经计划的问题是：

一旦落后，

人就开始：

* 焦虑；
* 补进度；
* 觉得失败；
* 最后彻底停止。

于是读经慢慢变成：

* KPI；
* 任务；
* 纪律考核。

我们认为应该更在意的，
不是：

# “你有没有完美坚持”

而是：

# “你有没有继续回来。”

> “你们亲近神，神就必亲近你们。”
> ——《雅各书》4:8

因此我们不强调：

* 打卡；
* 连续天数；
* 完成率；
* 阅读速度。

因为我们认为真正重要的，
不是表现，

而是关系。

---

## 3. 不补读，而是继续前进

### 解决：中断后的挫败感

很多人一旦停了：

* 三天；
* 一周；
* 一个月；

就会觉得：

“已经跟不上了。”

然后彻底放弃。

所以我们的原则很简单：

# 不补读，直接继续。

因为属灵生命不是考试。

没有人需要把“落下的灵修”补回来，
才能重新亲近神。

我们认为更重要的是：

# 今天重新开始。

---

## 4. 即使没有完成当天计划，也没有问题

### 解决：完美主义带来的属灵压力

有时候：

* 很忙；
* 很累；
* 情绪低落；
* 状态不好；

这时候如果觉得：

“我今天三章没读完。”

人很容易产生失败感。

于是连一章也不想读。

所以我们强调：

# 今天只读诗篇，也很好。

# 今天只读新约，也没有问题。

因为我们认为读经更重要的目标，
不是：

# “完成计划”

而是：

# “继续停留在神的话语里。”

有时候：

一句经文，
比三章快速读完更重要。

---

# 读经建议

我们推荐一种：

## 「三循环读经系统」

每天：

| 类型  | 内容        |
| --- | --------- |
| 旧约  | 1章（不含智慧书） |
| 新约  | 1章        |
| 智慧书 | 1篇 / 1章   |

三个部分独立循环，
读完后继续重新开始。

---

## 旧约循环

范围：

* 创世记 → 玛拉基书
  （不含约伯记、诗篇、箴言、传道书、雅歌）

旧约帮助我们认识：

* 神的计划；
* 历史；
* 律法；
* 先知；
* 应许。

---

## 新约循环

范围：

* 马太福音 → 启示录

耶稣来，
不是废掉律法，

而是：

# 成全律法。

> “莫想我来要废掉律法和先知；我来不是要废掉，乃是要成全。”
> ——《马太福音》5:17

而律法最终的核心，
不是规条，

而是：

# 爱。

> “你要尽心、尽性、尽意爱主你的神。
> 这是诫命中的第一，且是最大的。
> 其次也相仿，就是要爱人如己。
> 这两条诫命是律法和先知一切道理的总纲。”
> ——《马太福音》22:37–40

因此，

新约不断帮助我们：

* 回到基督；
* 回到恩典；
* 回到福音；
* 回到爱的关系。

---

## 智慧书循环

范围：

* 约伯记
* 诗篇
* 箴言
* 传道书
* 雅歌

智慧书帮助我们：

* 祷告；
* 默想；
* 敬拜；
* 面对真实人生。

它们不是理论，

而是：

# 人与神同行时真实的心声。

---

# 最后

我们最核心的目标，

不是帮助人：

# “快速读完整本圣经”

而是帮助人：

# 一次又一次回到神的话语里。

即使停了很久，

今天，
仍然可以重新开始。

en.title: Reflections on a Reading Plan
en.body:
# Returning to God’s Word

## A Reading Plan

> “But his delight is in the law of the Lord,
> and on his law he meditates day and night.”
> — Psalm 1:2

> “Man shall not live by bread alone,
> but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.”
> — Matthew 4:4

When many people begin reading Scripture,
they hope for:

* to know God more;
* to draw near to God more;
* to read through the whole Bible with seriousness.

But over time,
reading easily becomes:

* checking a box;
* a task;
* progress tracking;
* pressure.

Then:

* falling behind brings guilt;
* stopping leads to giving up;
* not finishing feels like failure.

We believe the deeper purpose of reading Scripture
has never been only:

# “finishing the reading.”

In our view, God’s word
is not mainly for adding religious knowledge,

but for:

# leading people back into a loving relationship with God.

> “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.”
> — Matthew 22:37

Therefore,

what we hope to build
is not a plan to:

# “finish the Bible quickly,”

but a rhythm of:

# long-term, steady, real walking with God.

---

# Our Approach

## 1. A Three-Cycle System

### Addressing: long-term imbalance, fatigue, and easy interruption in Bible reading

Many people fail at reading Scripture
not because they do not love God,

but because over time they read only one kind of content.

For example:

* reading Old Testament continuously becomes tiring;
* reading Law continuously becomes heavy;
* reading only familiar passages leads to stagnation.

So we use a pattern of:

* Old Testament
* New Testament
* Wisdom literature

all at the same time.

The Old Testament helps us know God’s plan and foundation;

the New Testament continually brings life back to Christ and the gospel;

Wisdom literature helps us pray, meditate, and walk with God in real life.

---

## 2. No Check-Ins, No Racing Ahead

### Addressing: guilt, pressure, and giving up

The problem with many reading plans is this:

once you fall behind,

people begin to:

* feel anxious;
* catch up frantically;
* feel they have failed;
* finally stop altogether.

Then reading slowly becomes:

* a KPI;
* a task;
* a discipline exam.

We believe what matters more
is not:

# “whether you kept a perfect streak”

but:

# “whether you keep coming back.”

> “Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.”
> — James 4:8

So we do not emphasize:

* check-ins;
* consecutive days;
* completion rate;
* reading speed.

Because we believe what truly matters
is not performance,

but relationship.

---

## 3. No Catch-Up—Keep Moving Forward

### Addressing: defeat after interruption

Once many people stop for:

* three days;
* a week;
* a month;

they feel:

“I can’t catch up anymore.”

Then they give up completely.

So our principle is simple:

# do not catch up—just continue.

Because spiritual life is not an exam.

No one needs to make up “missed devotion”
before they can draw near to God again.

We believe what matters more is:

# starting again today.

---

## 4. It Is Fine Even If You Do Not Finish Today’s Plan

### Addressing: spiritual pressure from perfectionism

Sometimes:

* very busy;
* very tired;
* low mood;
* not in a good state;

if you feel:

“I did not finish my three chapters today,”

failure easily follows.

Then you may not want to read even one chapter.

So we emphasize:

# reading only Psalms today is also good.

# reading only the New Testament today is also fine.

Because we believe the more important goal of reading
is not:

# “completing the plan”

but:

# “staying in God’s word.”

Sometimes:

one verse
matters more than three chapters read quickly.

---

# Our Reading Recommendation

We recommend:

## A Three-Cycle Reading System

Each day:

| Type | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Old Testament | 1 chapter (excluding Wisdom books) |
| New Testament | 1 chapter |
| Wisdom | 1 psalm / 1 chapter |

The three tracks cycle independently;
when finished, begin again.

---

## Old Testament Cycle

Scope:

* Genesis → Malachi
  (excluding Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Solomon)

The Old Testament helps us know:

* God’s plan;
* history;
* Law;
* the prophets;
* promise.

---

## New Testament Cycle

Scope:

* Matthew → Revelation

Jesus came
not to abolish the Law,

but:

# to fulfill the Law.

> “Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them.”
> — Matthew 5:17

And the heart of the Law
is not rules,

but:

# love.

> “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.
> This is the great and first commandment.
> And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
> On these two commandments depend all the Law and the Prophets.”
> — Matthew 22:37–40

Therefore,

the New Testament continually helps us:

* return to Christ;
* return to grace;
* return to the gospel;
* return to a relationship of love.

---

## Wisdom Literature Cycle

Scope:

* Job
* Psalms
* Proverbs
* Ecclesiastes
* Song of Solomon

Wisdom literature helps us:

* pray;
* meditate;
* worship;
* face real life.

They are not theory,

but:

# the honest voice of walking with God.

---

# In Closing

Our deepest goal

is not to help people:

# “read through the whole Bible quickly”

but to help people:

# return again and again to God’s word.

Even if you have stopped for a long time,

today,
you can still begin again.
